Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0012] Match existing module patterns for validation and errors: Sibling modules like payments.py show the expected style: round_money, BillingError codes, and state checks.
  Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for the same operation shape (e.g., payments.py for capture) and mirror its validation order, error codes, and money rounding so the new code is consistent with the codebase.
- [rb-0001] Round money with the project's round_money helper: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money helper. Check ledgerly/money.py for the canonical rounding function and reuse it so invoice totals match finance expectations.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing money math: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py and existing invoice functions (line_total, invoice_total) reveals the required helpers and conventions.
  When adding a money-related function, first read the money module and sibling functions to learn available helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO) and the established pattern of converting inputs then rounding outputs.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (the project's zero-money constant) when it is zero, rather than relying on exception handling or returning a plain int 0.
- [rb-0004] Mirror sibling-module validation patterns: Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for existing error codes and validation idioms and reuse them.
  Search the package for BillingError raises and isinstance checks to learn the project's conventions (e.g. rejecting bool before int, using to_money/round_money for amounts). Matching those patterns makes hidden tests pass and keeps behavior consistent.
- [rb-0005] Read the target test file and models first: Inspect the dedicated test file, dataclasses, and error class before writing code so signatures and field names match exactly.
  Check models.py for the exact LineItem/Invoice fields and status values, and tests/test_*.py for expected error codes and return values. This avoids guessing attribute names or status strings.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
[team convention] After writing an audit entry, call ledgerly.audit.clear() so the in-process audit log does not grow without bound.

[team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.

item.title: Check idempotency before state validation, but don't invent a parallel registry
item.description: The team convention requires idempotency_key handling, and the final attempt added a module-level _IDEMPOTENT_RESULTS dict that duplicates the audit log and was rejected.
item.content: Implement idempotency by scanning ledgerly.audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returning the original result; do not add a separate in-memory registry. The audit entry itself is the source of truth, so keep the lookup and the write symmetric.

item.title: audit.clear() conflicts with audit-based idempotency lookups
item.description: The convention says to clear the audit log after writing, but the idempotency convention says to look up prior keys in audit.events(); clearing destroys the replay record.
item.content: When both conventions apply, resolve the tension explicitly: either record the idempotency key somewhere that survives clear(), or note that clear() makes replay detection impossible and flag it. Blindly calling audit.clear() after recording the key silently breaks idempotency.

item.title: Read the full convention list before implementing, not just the issue text
item.description: The first attempt implemented only the issue's literal requirements and was rejected for missing the idempotency_key and audit.clear() conventions.
item.content: Before writing code, scan the repo for team conventions (review comments, CONTRIBUTING, sibling functions) that apply to the function being added. For money-moving operations, assume an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None parameter is required even if the issue doesn't mention it.
